Brief should we wrapped in a line.
Done
can we follow camel case for api names?
Done
Wrap brief in a single line.
Done
can we have it as inline function ?
Done

This is not the correct place to call this API.
The property can get set to completed while these collections are going on and this can cause issues.
I agree. Moving this call to just before setting "CollectionStatus" = "Completed".
Done
I dont see a reason why Manager should hold this API. If you have any thought here, please let me know else let worker host this API which can be called by Manager.
`Manager` should process the list of failed EEPROMs and retry collection of these FRUs (by `CollectSingleFruVpd()` or some other API).
Done

why are you clearing the container?
if you did this for suppressing the unused variable warning, then I would suggest you to use [[maybe_unused]] attribute in front of the variable declaration.
nit: getFailedEepromPaths() sounds better.
`getFailedEepromPaths()` can be misleading and may be interpreted as failed EEPROMs, which is not the case here.

If `m_failedEepromPaths` is not empty (meaning thread creation failed for some EEPROM), we do not want "CollectionStatus" property to become "Completed". This is handled in `worker.cpp` line 1520.
 As of this PR, `processFailedEeproms()` is partially implemented and if we actually get an exception while calling `std::thread()`, "CollectionStatus" would never become "Completed". So for now, `processFailedEeproms()` simply clears the container.
Done
Done
once you retry the vpd collection for those failed eeproms and if it succeeds then you should have a mechanism to clear the m_failedEepromPaths from worker class.
Yes. This is a TODO. We discussed and decided to take this part later on.
Done

why not push_back here?

when we try to recollect the vpd we can start from the one which failed first. this will give some time for the eeprom which failed last to get into a readable state if it can.

"this will give some time for the eeprom which failed last to get into a readable state if it can." Can you please clarify on this point?

This implementation is to handle a `std::thread()` failure, which is a firmware issue, and not because of any faulty EEPROM state.
Done
we should log a critical PEL here as we don't have any other way to identify it later.
I agree. This is a double failure scenario though. @sunnsr25@in.ibm.com, what do you think?
We discussed this and have decided not to log any PELs here.
API to process EEPROMs whose VPD collection failed while launching thread. ?
As @brief should be wrapped in single line, so used a more concise language here.
ok

getFailedEepromPaths() is enough I guess, as paths says its multiple.
And the description of the API will tell its from thread launching failure.

this also matches with member variable 'm_failedEepromPaths' as a get method.
getFailedEepromPaths() can be misinterpreted as "EEPROM paths which have failed", but in reality this returns a list of EEPROMs for which the thread launching has failed.

then should we rename variable m_failedEepromPaths as well ?
I don't think so, the description of the API/variable tells what it is doing.
Its fine to keep this way, but this what I am thinking.
Addressed
It should be trigger VPD collection for each failed EEPROM paths, not for object paths under the EEPROM path in JSON.
Done

I don't agree with these nested try/catch.
If required can be at the function level.
Done
API to get list of EEPROMs for which thread creation failed?
Done
